required_transformation: Inflation-adjust nominal IDR/day to a common price period using geographically compatible CPI where defensible.
critical_caveats: The 2023 observation is a Jabodetabek purposive sample; the 2025 observation has broader purposive coverage with an internal 62/67-locality discrepancy. Sampling frames and geography differ.
allowed_use: Caveated comparison of source-sample gross daily earnings after documented inflation treatment.
prohibited_use: National trend inference; direct welfare conclusion; unadjusted nominal level comparison.
rationale: Economic concept and daily time basis align, but monetary periods differ and sample/geography are not equivalent.

required_transformation: Inflation-adjust recalled nominal IDR/day values to a common price period if level comparison is performed.
critical_caveats: All values are retrospective recall from longer-tenure respondents interviewed in 2023; they are not independent historical survey waves.
allowed_use: Caveated within-source recalled trajectory or sensitivity context.
prohibited_use: Treating 2018-2019, 2020-2021, and 2022-2023 as repeated cross-sections or panel waves.
rationale: Source question and subgroup lineage are common, but recall and nominal monetary periods prevent direct historical-wave comparison.

required_transformation: None in Stage 2; nominal bracket thresholds cannot be converted to real-income brackets without microdata.
critical_caveats: Income layer is unspecified; pre-pandemic and pandemic values are retrospective recall; fixed nominal brackets do not represent constant purchasing-power thresholds.
allowed_use: Within-source comparison of reported nominal income-category distributions with explicit recall and bracket caveats.
prohibited_use: Mapping to gross/net earnings; real-income distribution comparison; independent-wave interpretation.
rationale: The category structure is consistent within SRC010, but semantic and temporal limitations remain material.

metric_concept: daily income versus explicit gross earnings
critical_caveats: SRC010 income layer is unspecified and reported as a distribution; IDEAS observations are explicit gross means.
prohibited_use: Numerical gross-earnings comparison or pooled estimate.
rationale: Economic layer and statistic type do not match.

metric_concept: fuel plus food/drink daily cost bundle
required_transformation: Inflation-adjust nominal IDR/day to a common price period if comparing amounts.
critical_caveats: The bundle includes food/drink, which is outside project operating costs; geography and purposive sample coverage differ.
allowed_use: Caveated comparison of the source-defined mixed bundle after inflation treatment.
prohibited_use: Treating the bundle as project operating cost or using it directly for project net operating earnings.
rationale: Source-defined bundle and daily mean basis are similar, but monetary period and sample/geography require treatment and caveats.

metric_concept: fuel plus food/drink share of gross earnings
required_transformation: None required for the reported percentage itself.
critical_caveats: The source-defined bundle includes personal food/drink; geography and purposive sample coverage differ.
allowed_use: Caveated comparison of the source-defined bundle-to-gross ratio.
prohibited_use: Calling the percentage project operating-cost share or applying it outside the source-defined bundle.
rationale: The ratio concept is aligned within the IDEAS source family, but cost-boundary and sample differences remain.

critical_caveats: The 2020 and 2023 observations are Jabodetabek purposive samples; 2025 has broader purposive coverage. Survey periods and respondent composition differ.
allowed_use: Sample-level descriptive comparison of exact seven-day workweek prevalence.
prohibited_use: National prevalence trend or causal interpretation.
rationale: Category, time basis, unit, vehicle universe, and broad work concept align, but sample and geography do not.

critical_caveats: Driver-reported categories are not transaction-level realized deductions; geography, period, and purposive samples differ.
allowed_use: Sample-level comparison of reported 20% deduction prevalence.
prohibited_use: Realized commission rate comparison; legal-compliance conclusion; transaction-level deduction estimate.
rationale: The reported category is similar across the two IDEAS surveys, but evidence layer and sample scope constrain interpretation.

critical_caveats: One source reports a mean while others report nonmatching distribution thresholds; all are generic source-reported working time rather than proven online/productive hours.
prohibited_use: Pooled mean working hours or direct prevalence comparison across nonmatching thresholds.
rationale: Statistic type and threshold definitions differ materially.

critical_caveats: Thresholds differ (>8, 12, 9-16, 61-112/week, 9-12/day); daily and weekly bases differ; samples and geographies differ.
allowed_use: Qualitative context that long source-reported working-time schedules appear in multiple studies.
prohibited_use: Exact cross-source prevalence ranking or pooled percentage.
rationale: The observations address related workload concepts but are not numerically aligned.

critical_caveats: SRC029 reports a mean; SRC013 reports selected brackets and does not provide complete microdata for mean reconstruction.
prohibited_use: Direct mean comparison or reconstructed mean from incomplete bracket shares.
rationale: Statistic types and available distribution detail are incompatible.

critical_caveats: SRC029 reports a mean; SRC013 reports selected brackets; distance basis is unresolved as paid-trip versus total work-related distance.
allowed_use: Separate source-specific distance description with basis caveat.
prohibited_use: Fuel-cost allocation using these values as total work distance; direct mean comparison.
rationale: Statistic type differs and the distance concept is not sufficiently resolved.

critical_caveats: SRC030 cost basis is unresolved; SRC013 net subtracts a mixed fuel-plus-food/drink bundle; one is a daily distribution and the other a monthly source estimate.
allowed_use: Separate description of each source-defined net concept.
prohibited_use: Project net operating earnings comparison or time-basis conversion as if definitions matched.
rationale: Cost boundaries, statistic types, and time bases are materially different.

critical_caveats: SRC013 measures program availability and receipt frequency; SRC017 measures ever/never receipt experience. Denominators also differ or are unresolved.
prohibited_use: Direct bonus-prevalence comparison or monetary incentive inference.
rationale: The survey questions measure different incentive concepts.

critical_caveats: SRC017 contains stated preference/perception; SRC013/SRC029 contain driver-reported deduction categories; none are matched transaction evidence.
allowed_use: Contextual comparison of evidence layers while keeping them separate.
prohibited_use: Converting preferences or perceptions into realized deduction estimates.
rationale: Related commission topics exist, but evidence types are not interchangeable.

metric_concept: gross earnings plus available cost evidence
critical_caveats: Available cost observations are mixed fuel-plus-food/drink bundles and the same-observation chain does not include complete operating costs and realized deductions.
prohibited_use: Constructing project net operating earnings from these components.
rationale: The project accounting chain is incomplete and the cost boundary is incompatible with project net operating earnings.

metric_concept: normative/platform policy versus driver deduction evidence
required_transformation: Scope and effective-date matching would be required in later regulatory reconciliation.
critical_caveats: Standardized driver evidence is self-reported; Stage 2 reference inputs are normative/platform-stated rather than matched realized transactions.
allowed_use: Layered regulatory context and later reconciliation with explicit evidence labels.
prohibited_use: Legal compliance conclusion or assumption that ceilings/stated rates equal realized deductions.
rationale: Normative, company-stated, and driver-reported evidence answer different questions.
